healthcareSystem: Public healthcare system severely degraded by years of conflict. Private clinics in Tripoli and Misrata offer better care. Many Libyan doctors trained abroad but facilities are poorly equipped.
qualityNotes: Healthcare quality varies dramatically by location. Tripoli and Misrata have functioning private clinics. Rural areas and conflict-affected regions have almost no healthcare. Many qualified doctors have left the country.
pharmacyHours: Typically 9am-9pm in major cities. Reduced availability on Fridays. Look for 'صيدلية' (Saydaliyya).
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies in Tripoli stock many common medications but supply chains are unreliable. Counterfeit medications are a concern. Bring essential medications from home.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is inconsistent. Many medications available over the counter that would require prescriptions elsewhere. Drug quality cannot always be guaranteed.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic painkillers
restrictedMeds.note: Opioid medications are strictly controlled. Carry original prescriptions and a doctor's letter in Arabic or English.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Benzodiazepines and similar medications require documentation. Islamic law influences drug regulations.

restrictedMeds.name: Alcohol-based medications
restrictedMeds.note: Alcohol is prohibited in Libya. Medications containing alcohol may be confiscated at customs.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English and Arabic listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. Carry extra supplies as local availability is unreliable.

travelInsurance.tips: Medical evacuation coverage is essential. Many standard travel insurance policies exclude Libya due to security concerns — verify coverage explicitly. Ensure evacuation to Tunisia or Europe is covered.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for entry. Malaria is not a significant risk. Ensure routine vaccinations are current. Consult a travel medicine clinic before traveling.

waterNotes: Tap water quality is inconsistent. Bottled water is recommended, especially outside major cities. Desalination plants provide water in coastal areas but quality varies.
foodSafetyTips: Eat at established restaurants in major cities. Avoid raw vegetables and unpeeled fruits from street vendors. Libyan cuisine is generally safe when freshly prepared and served hot.
medicalTourismNote: Libya is not a medical tourism destination. Libyans frequently travel to Tunisia, Turkey, or Europe for medical procedures.
metaDescription: Health guide for Libya. Emergency numbers, pharmacy info, travel insurance advice, vaccination tips, and medical evacuation guidance for travelers.

hospitals.name: Tripoli Medical Center
hospitals.notes: Largest hospital in Libya. Has some English-speaking doctors trained abroad. Facilities are functional but may lack supplies.

hospitals.name: Misrata Medical Center
hospitals.notes: Major hospital in Libya's third-largest city. Some English-speaking physicians available.

hospitals.name: Libya General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Government facility. Limited English. Bring a translator app.

pharmacyPhrases.phrase: عندي ألم في المعدة (Indi alam fil-ma'ida)

dentalCare.availability: Private dental clinics available in Tripoli and Misrata. Limited elsewhere.
dentalCare.notes: Private dental clinics in Tripoli offer reasonable care. Equipment may not meet Western standards. Sterilization practices vary.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, seek private clinics in Tripoli. For complex procedures, evacuation to Tunisia is advisable.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No national mental health crisis line
mentalHealth.internationalLine: Contact your embassy or International SOS
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited — some private practitioners in Tripoli
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are extremely limited and carry social stigma. No formal crisis support infrastructure exists. Pre-arrange remote therapy options.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Very limited accessibility infrastructure. Most buildings lack ramps and elevators.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Major hospitals in Tripoli have basic wheelchair access. Most facilities are not adapted.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transportation. Private vehicle with driver required.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Libya is challenging for travelers with mobility limitations. Plan for private assistance throughout your stay.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Limited COVID testing available at major hospitals in Tripoli.
covidStatus.notes: Healthcare capacity is limited for any respiratory illness. Bring personal protective supplies.

insuranceClaimProcess: Cash payment is required at most facilities. Collect detailed receipts and medical reports. Many private clinics can provide English-language documentation. File claims with your insurer upon return.

commonCosts.note: Private healthcare costs are moderate by international standards. Public facilities are cheaper but quality is poor. Cash payment expected.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation is essential for serious conditions. Tripoli and Misrata airports can handle medevac flights. Security situation may complicate evacuation logistics.

pharmacyChains.name: Private pharmacies
pharmacyChains.identifier: Look for green cross or 'صيدلية' sign

drugNameMap.note: Available in well-stocked pharmacies. Bring your own to be safe.
